extName.description: The extension name, shown in the browser and on the store listings.

extDescription.message: Every Nexus mod tile gets a compatibility verdict for the game build you actually play, so you can filter down to what will run.
extDescription.description: The store short description. Chrome caps this at 132 characters, so a translation must stay under it.

background_errorTimeoutSeconds.message: The request took longer than $seconds$s and was abandoned.
background_errorTimeoutSeconds.description: Shown when a request to Nexus or Steam is cut off by the extension's own timer. Reaches the popup and the on-page report. The number is whole seconds and 's' is the unit abbreviation.

background_errorRateLimitedUntil.message: Nexus API limit reached. It resets at $resetTime$.
background_errorRateLimitedUntil.description: Shown when Nexus answers 429, or when the daily quota is spent and the wait is too long, and Nexus told the extension when the quota resets. Reaches the popup and the on-page report.

background_errorRateLimited.message: Nexus API limit reached. Checks resume once the limit resets.
background_errorRateLimited.description: Shown when Nexus answers 429 and did not say when the quota resets. Reaches the popup and the on-page report.

background_errorRateLimitedShort.description: Shown when the extension stops before sending a request because the daily quota is spent and no reset time is known. Reaches the popup and the on-page report.

background_errorInvalidKey.message: Nexus rejected your API key. Re-enter it in the extension popup.
background_errorInvalidKey.description: Shown when Nexus answers 401. The user's saved API key is wrong or revoked. Reaches the popup and the on-page report.

background_errorForbidden.message: Nexus refused this request. A premium account or an active nexusmods.com login may be required.
background_errorForbidden.description: Shown when Nexus answers 403. Reaches the popup and the on-page report.

background_errorNotFound.message: Nexus has no such mod for this game (deleted, hidden, or wrong game).
background_errorNotFound.description: Shown when Nexus answers 404 for a mod the user is looking at. Reaches the popup and the on-page report.

background_errorServerError.message: Nexus is not responding right now (HTTP $status$).
background_errorServerError.description: Shown when Nexus answers with a 5xx status. Reaches the popup and the on-page report. The number is the raw HTTP status code and stays as digits.

background_errorBadRequest.description: Shown when Nexus answers with a 4xx status the extension has no specific wording for. Reaches the popup and the on-page report. The detail is up to 120 characters of Nexus's own untranslated response body, already prefixed with a space, and is empty when Nexus sent no body.

background_errorTimeout.message: The request took too long and was abandoned.
background_errorTimeout.description: Shown when a request was aborted for taking too long and no duration is known. Reaches the popup and the on-page report.

background_errorOffline.description: Shown when the browser could not reach Nexus at all, usually because the machine is offline. Reaches the popup and the on-page report.

background_errorDisabled.description: Shown when the user has turned the extension off in the popup and something still asks it to check a mod. Reaches the popup and the on-page report.

background_errorUnexpected.description: Shown when a failure carried no readable text of its own. The last-resort error wording. Reaches the popup and the on-page report.

background_errorNoApiKey.message: API key not found. Add your Nexus API key in the extension popup.
background_errorNoApiKey.description: Shown when the user has not saved a Nexus API key yet and asks for something that needs one, such as a download or a file list. Reaches the popup and the on-page report.

background_errorDownloadLinkMissing.description: Shown when Nexus answered a download request but the answer carried no usable address, so the download cannot start. Reaches the on-page download report.

background_errorNxmLinkMissing.description: Shown when the user downloads through a mod manager and the Nexus download page did not contain the nxm:// handoff link. Reaches the on-page download report.

background_errorNoEligibleFiles.message: No eligible files found for this mod.
background_errorNoEligibleFiles.description: Shown when a mod has no file the extension is willing to download, for example when only archived files remain and the user has not opted into old files. Reaches the on-page download report.

background_errorLayoutUnrecognized.message: Could not read this mod page's requirements section. The Nexus page layout is not one NMA recognizes.
background_errorLayoutUnrecognized.description: Shown when the extension loaded a mod page to read its requirements and the page markup was not one it knows. NMA is the extension's short name and is not translated.

background_errorNavigationChanged.description: Shown in place of a verdict when the user navigated away before the check for a mod finished, so the answer no longer belongs to the page on screen. A short phrase, not a sentence.

background_errorNotConfigured.message: Nexus Mods Assistant needs $missing$ before it can check mods. Open the extension popup to finish setup.
background_errorNotConfigured.description: Shown on every mod tile when setup is incomplete. The inserted text is the list of missing items, built from background_setupNeedsApiKey, background_setupNeedsGame and background_setupNeedsVersion joined by background_setupNeedsJoin. Nexus Mods Assistant is the product name and is not translated.

missing.example: an API key and a game version

background_setupNeedsApiKey.description: One item in the list of missing setup steps inserted into background_errorNotConfigured. Lower case, no period: it appears mid-sentence.

background_setupNeedsGame.description: One item in the list of missing setup steps inserted into background_errorNotConfigured, meaning the user has not chosen which game to check mods for. Lower case, no period: it appears mid-sentence.

background_setupNeedsVersion.description: One item in the list of missing setup steps inserted into background_errorNotConfigured, meaning the user has not said which game build they play. Lower case, no period: it appears mid-sentence.

background_setupNeedsJoin.description: Joins the last two items in the list of missing setup steps for background_errorNotConfigured. The first insert is everything before the last item, already separated by commas; the second is the last item.

background_errorGameMismatch.message: This page is $pageGame$, but NMA is set up for $configuredGame$. Switch game in the extension popup to check these mods.
background_errorGameMismatch.description: Shown on every mod tile when the user is browsing one game's mods while the extension is configured for another. Both inserts are Nexus game domain names such as gamedomain and are never translated. NMA is the extension's short name.

background_errorVersionUnreadable.message: NMA cannot read "$version$" as a game version, so it cannot judge any mod against it. Set a numeric version such as 1.6.1170 in the extension popup.
background_errorVersionUnreadable.description: Shown on every mod tile when the game version the user typed in the popup is not something the extension can parse. The insert is whatever the user typed. NMA is the extension's short name and 1.6.1170 is a sample build number; keep both as they are.

background_errorNoVersionDerived.message: No public source names a game version for $gameDomain$, so NMA cannot tell a game version from a mod version here. That is a gap in the data rather than in the extension, and it is the same for everyone. Type the version you play in the extension popup to check anyway.
background_errorNoVersionDerived.description: Shown on every mod tile for a game whose build numbers no public source states, so the extension has nothing to compare mods against. The insert is a Nexus game domain name such as gamedomain and is never translated. NMA is the extension's short name.

background_errorNoVersionSource.message: No version source could be reached, so nothing could be derived for this game yet.
background_errorNoVersionSource.description: Shown in the popup when the user refreshes the game version list and not one of the sources the extension asks answered, usually because the machine is offline.

background_errorNoGameDomain.message: A game domain is needed before versions can be derived for it.
background_errorNoGameDomain.description: Shown in the popup when a request for a game's version list arrives without a valid game, for example before the user has picked one.

background_errorNoStoreListing.message: No store listing matches that game closely enough to be certain, so none was stored.
background_errorNoStoreListing.description: Shown in the popup when the user asks the extension to find the game's Steam store page and no candidate matched well enough to trust. Nothing is saved rather than risk binding the wrong game.

background_sourceFileVersion.description: Names where a game version was found, and is inserted at the START of background_verdictStatedInRange and its three siblings: 'A file version states "1.6.1170", ...'. Capitalized because it opens the sentence. This one means the version field of one of the mod's uploaded files.

background_sourceFileName.description: Names where a game version was found, and is inserted at the START of background_verdictStatedInRange and its three siblings. Capitalized because it opens the sentence. This one means the name of one of the mod's uploaded files.

background_sourceChangelog.description: Names where a game version was found, and is inserted at the START of background_verdictStatedInRange and its three siblings. Capitalized because it opens the sentence. This one means the mod's changelog on Nexus.

background_sourceDescription.description: Names where a game version was found, and is inserted at the START of background_verdictStatedInRange and its three siblings. Capitalized because it opens the sentence. This one means the mod's description text on Nexus.

background_sourceUploadDate.description: Names where a game version was found, and is inserted at the START of background_verdictStatedInRange and its three siblings. Capitalized because it opens the sentence. This one means the date the mod's newest file was uploaded.

background_sourceNone.description: Names where a game version was found when nothing was found at all, and is inserted at the START of background_verdictStatedInRange and its three siblings. Capitalized because it opens the sentence. Unreachable from the verdict sentences: this source is set only on the no-evidence result, never on evidence that was found, so it never appears as the subject of background_verdictStatedInRange or its siblings.

background_verdictPartialNote.message: One source could not be read ($cause$), so this check is partial.
background_verdictPartialNote.description: Appended to a compatibility verdict when the extension reached a conclusion while one of its evidence sources failed to load. The insert is another error message from this same catalog, such as background_errorTimeout.

cause.example: The request took too long and was abandoned.

background_verdictUploadDateInRange.message: No game version is stated anywhere, but the newest file was uploaded on $uploadDate$, after game version $gameVersion$. Inferred, not confirmed.
background_verdictUploadDateInRange.description: The tooltip explaining a 'likely compatible' verdict reached only from how recently the mod was updated. The first insert is a date in YYYY-MM-DD form, the second a game build number.

background_verdictStatedInRange.message: $source$ states "$evidence$", which is inside your selected range.
background_verdictStatedInRange.description: The tooltip explaining a 'compatible' verdict. The first insert names where the version was found (one of the background_source* entries, already capitalized, so this sentence opens with it); the second is the exact text found on the mod page.

background_verdictMentionedInRange.message: $source$ mentions "$evidence$", which is inside your selected range. That is an inference, not a stated game version.
background_verdictMentionedInRange.description: The tooltip explaining a 'likely compatible' verdict, where the number was only mentioned in passing rather than stated as the supported game version. The first insert names where it was found (one of the background_source* entries, already capitalized, so this sentence opens with it); the second is the exact text found.

background_verdictUploadDateOutOfRange.message: No game version is stated anywhere, and the newest file's upload date ($uploadDate$) does not place it inside your selected range.
background_verdictUploadDateOutOfRange.description: The tooltip explaining an 'incompatible' verdict reached only from how recently the mod was updated. The insert is a date in YYYY-MM-DD form.

background_verdictStatedOutOfRange.message: $source$ states "$evidence$", the newest game version this mod mentions, and it is outside your selected range.
background_verdictStatedOutOfRange.description: The tooltip explaining an 'incompatible' verdict. The first insert names where the version was found (one of the background_source* entries, already capitalized, so this sentence opens with it); the second is the exact text found on the mod page.

background_verdictMentionedOutOfRange.message: $source$ mentions "$evidence$", the newest game version this mod mentions, and it is outside your selected range. That is an inference, not a stated game version.
background_verdictMentionedOutOfRange.description: The tooltip explaining an 'incompatible' verdict where the number was only mentioned in passing rather than stated as the supported game version. The first insert names where it was found (one of the background_source* entries, already capitalized, so this sentence opens with it); the second is the exact text found.

background_verdictNoVersionDataDeep.message: This mod names no game version in its files, changelog or description.
background_verdictNoVersionDataDeep.description: The tooltip explaining an 'unknown' verdict after the extension opened the mod's file list as well as its text and still found no game version.

background_verdictNoVersionDataShallow.message: This mod names no game version in its description or changelog. Its files were not opened for this check.
background_verdictNoVersionDataShallow.description: The tooltip explaining an 'unknown' verdict from a quick check that read only the mod's text. Opening the file list costs an extra request and happens only for the mod page the user is on.

background_storeNoteSearchFailed.message: The store search did not answer, so store sources were skipped.
background_storeNoteSearchFailed.description: Appended in the popup to the report on a game version refresh, explaining that the Steam store search did not respond, so the publisher's own build numbers were not read this time.

background_storeNoteNoMatch.message: No store listing matched this game closely enough to be sure, so store sources were skipped.
background_storeNoteNoMatch.description: Appended in the popup to the report on a game version refresh, explaining that no Steam listing matched the game well enough to trust, so the publisher's own build numbers were not read.

background_storeNoteRecordUnreadable.message: The store record for this game could not be read, so store sources were skipped this time.
background_storeNoteRecordUnreadable.description: Appended in the popup to the report on a game version refresh, explaining that the Steam page for the matched game could not be loaded on this attempt.

background_storeNoteNotAGame.message: The closest store listing is not a game entry, so store sources were skipped rather than read another product's builds.
background_storeNoteNotAGame.description: Appended in the popup to the report on a game version refresh, explaining that the closest Steam match was something other than a game, such as a soundtrack or a demo, so it was refused.

background_storeNoteWrongApp.message: The closest store listing belongs to another app, so store sources were skipped.
background_storeNoteWrongApp.description: Appended in the popup to the report on a game version refresh, explaining that the Steam listing that came back is for a different application than the one that was asked for.

background_storeNoteDifferentGame.message: The store listing names a different game than the catalog does, so store sources were skipped.
background_storeNoteDifferentGame.description: Appended in the popup to the report on a game version refresh, explaining that the Steam page's own title does not match the game name in the Nexus catalog, so the binding was refused.

background_ssoConnecting.description: The status line under the Authorize button in the popup, while the extension opens its connection to the Nexus Mods sign-in service. SSO is the sign-in feature's own name on Nexus and is not translated.

background_ssoWaitingApproval.message: Waiting for your approval in the Nexus Mods tab...
background_ssoWaitingApproval.description: The status line under the Authorize button in the popup, after a Nexus Mods tab has opened and the user has to approve the extension there.

background_ssoHandshakeFailed.message: Failed to initiate the SSO handshake.
background_ssoHandshakeFailed.description: The status line under the Authorize button in the popup, shown as an error when the connection opened but the opening request could not be sent. SSO is the sign-in feature's own name on Nexus.

background_ssoConnectionFailed.description: The status line under the Authorize button in the popup, shown as an error when the connection to the Nexus sign-in service could not be opened at all. SSO is the sign-in feature's own name on Nexus.

background_ssoRejected.description: The status line under the Authorize button in the popup, shown as an error when Nexus refused the sign-in attempt without saying why. SSO is the sign-in feature's own name on Nexus.

background_ssoConnectionReady.description: The status line under the Authorize button in the popup, once the sign-in connection is established and the only remaining step is the user approving it on the Nexus Mods tab.

background_ssoComplete.description: The status line under the Authorize button in the popup, on success: Nexus sent an API key and the extension stored it. SSO is the sign-in feature's own name on Nexus.

background_ssoUnexpectedResponse.description: The status line under the Authorize button in the popup, shown as an error when the sign-in service sent something the extension could not read. SSO is the sign-in feature's own name on Nexus.

background_ssoLostConnection.message: Lost connection to SSO after multiple retries.
background_ssoLostConnection.description: The status line under the Authorize button in the popup, shown as an error after every reconnection attempt to the Nexus sign-in service has failed. SSO is the sign-in feature's own name on Nexus.

background_ssoReconnecting.description: The status line under the Authorize button in the popup, while the extension retries a dropped connection to the Nexus sign-in service. Both inserts are counts.

background_ssoCanceled.description: The status line under the Authorize button in the popup, after the user stops the sign-in flow themselves. SSO is the sign-in feature's own name on Nexus.

content_statusCompatible.description: Compatibility verdict shown on a mod tile badge, in the requirements table and in the filter bar. Means the mod states a version that matches the game build the user plays.

content_statusLikelyCompatible.description: Compatibility verdict shown on a mod tile badge, in the requirements table and in the filter bar. Means the match was inferred from weaker evidence than an exact version, so it is probable but not certain.

content_statusIncompatible.description: Compatibility verdict shown on a mod tile badge, in the requirements table and in the filter bar. Means the mod states a version that does not match the game build the user plays.

content_statusUnknown.description: Compatibility verdict shown on a mod tile badge, in the requirements table and in the filter bar. It means the check ran successfully and the mod simply does not state any version. Keep it distinct from content_statusFailed, which means the check could not run at all: found nothing versus could not look. Do not merge the two into one word.

content_statusFailed.description: Compatibility verdict shown on a mod tile badge, in the requirements table and in the filter bar. It means the check could not be performed (network, API or permission problem), so nothing is known either way. Keep it distinct from content_statusUnknown, which means the check ran and the mod stated no version: could not look versus found nothing. Do not merge the two into one word.

content_statusNotConfigured.description: Compatibility verdict shown on a mod tile badge when the user has not yet chosen a game version in the extension popup, so no verdict can be computed. This is a state of the extension, not a judgment about the mod.

content_statusFallbackUnknown.description: Badge text used when the check returned a verdict name the extension does not recognize, so no proper label exists for it.

content_evidenceFileVersion.description: Named in the badge tooltip after 'Evidence:'. The version was read from the mod file's own version field.

content_evidenceFileName.description: Named in the badge tooltip after 'Evidence:'. The version was read out of the mod file's name.

content_evidenceChangelog.description: Named in the badge tooltip after 'Evidence:'. The version was read from the mod's changelog.

content_evidenceDescription.description: Named in the badge tooltip after 'Evidence:'. The version was read from the mod's description text.

content_evidenceUploadDate.description: Named in the badge tooltip after 'Evidence:'. The version was inferred from when the file was uploaded.

content_evidenceNone.description: Named in the badge tooltip after 'Evidence:'. Nothing about the mod indicated a version.

content_confidenceExact.description: Named in the badge tooltip after 'Confidence:'. The detected version matched the played build exactly.

content_confidenceInferred.description: Named in the badge tooltip after 'Confidence:'. The verdict was deduced rather than read directly.

content_confidenceNone.description: Named in the badge tooltip after 'Confidence:'. No confidence level could be assigned.

content_tooltipDetectedVersion.description: Line in the compatibility badge tooltip naming the mod version the extension found.

content_tooltipEvidence.description: Line in the compatibility badge tooltip naming where the version was read from. The value is one of the content_evidence* strings.

content_tooltipConfidence.description: Line in the compatibility badge tooltip naming how sure the verdict is. The value is one of the content_confidence* strings.

content_tooltipMatched.description: Line in the compatibility badge tooltip quoting the snippet of mod text the version was read from.

content_badgeStatusVersion.description: Compatibility badge text: the verdict followed by the mod version that was detected.

content_badgeStatusReason.description: Compatibility badge text used when a check failed: the verdict followed by a short reason.

content_badgeNotConfigured.description: Compatibility badge text shown before the user has chosen which game build they play.

content_badgeDownloadNote.description: Compatibility badge text after a download was started: the badge keeps its previous text and gains a note about the download.

content_versionNotReported.description: Stands in for the mod version on a tile badge when the check found no version to show.

content_versionNotReportedShort.description: Stands in for the mod version in the narrow Compatibility column of a mod page's requirements table when the check found no version to show.

content_checking.description: Placeholder in the Compatibility column of a mod page's requirements table while that requirement is being checked.

content_checkingCompatibility.description: Placeholder on a mod tile badge while its compatibility check is running.

content_scrollToCheck.description: Badge text on a mod tile that is off screen: its check is deliberately deferred until it becomes visible.

content_scrollToCheckDetail.message: This mod is checked when it scrolls into view.
content_scrollToCheckDetail.description: Tooltip on the 'Scroll to check' badge, explaining why no verdict is shown yet.

content_noResponse.description: Tooltip reason on a mod tile badge when the compatibility check returned nothing at all.

content_compatibilityColumn.description: Heading of the extra column the extension adds to the requirements table on a Nexus mod page.

content_setVersionInPopup.message: Set the game version in the extension popup to get a verdict.
content_setVersionInPopup.description: Tooltip on the 'Not set up' badge on a mod page and in the requirements table, telling the user how to enable verdicts.

content_pickVersionInPopup.message: Pick the game version in the popup to get a verdict for this mod.
content_pickVersionInPopup.description: Tooltip on the 'Not set up' badge on a mod tile in the grid, telling the user how to enable verdicts.

content_filesButton.description: Button on a mod's compatibility badge that opens the list of that mod's downloadable files.

content_filesButtonForMod.description: Screen reader name for the Files button, naming which mod it belongs to.

content_filesButtonForThisMod.description: Screen reader name for the Files button on a mod tile whose name is not known yet.

content_filesButtonForRequiredMod.description: Screen reader name for the Files button in the requirements table when the required mod's name is not known yet.

content_filesDropdownLabel.description: Screen reader name for the panel that opens under a mod badge listing its files.

content_filesLoading.description: Placeholder inside the file list panel while the mod's files are being fetched.

content_filesFetchFailed.description: Reason shown inside the file list panel when the request for a mod's files came back with no usable answer and no reason of its own.

content_filesLoadFailed.message: Could not load the file list: $REASON$
content_filesLoadFailed.description: Message replacing the file list panel's contents when the files could not be fetched.

content_couldNotLoadFileList.message: Could not load the file list
content_couldNotLoadFileList.description: Badge text on a mod tile when a download could not start because the mod's file list could not be fetched.

content_fileListUnreadable.message: The file list could not be read.
content_fileListUnreadable.description: Reason given when the answer to a request for a mod's files was not in a shape the extension could read.

content_fileCategoryMain.description: Name of a Nexus file category. Used as a heading in the file list panel and the file picker dialog. Keep this in English in every locale: it is the heading nexusmods.com prints on its own Files tab, and this panel mirrors that grouping, so a reader comparing the two must see the same words.

content_fileCategoryUpdate.description: Name of a Nexus file category. Used as a heading in the file list panel and the file picker dialog, and as the label of the filter-bar checkbox that shows or hides those files. Keep this in English in every locale: it is the heading nexusmods.com prints on its own Files tab, and this panel mirrors that grouping, so a reader comparing the two must see the same words.

content_fileCategoryOptional.description: Name of a Nexus file category. Used as a heading in the file list panel and the file picker dialog, and as the label of the filter-bar checkbox that shows or hides those files. Keep this in English in every locale: it is the heading nexusmods.com prints on its own Files tab, and this panel mirrors that grouping, so a reader comparing the two must see the same words.

content_fileCategoryMisc.description: Name of a Nexus file category. Used as a heading in the file list panel and the file picker dialog, and as the label of the filter-bar checkbox that shows or hides those files. Keep this in English in every locale: it is the heading nexusmods.com prints on its own Files tab, and this panel mirrors that grouping, so a reader comparing the two must see the same words.

content_fileCategoryOld.description: Name of a Nexus file category covering old versions and archived files. Used as a heading in the file list panel and the file picker dialog, and as the label of the filter-bar checkbox that shows or hides those files. Keep this in English in every locale: it is the heading nexusmods.com prints on its own Files tab, and this panel mirrors that grouping, so a reader comparing the two must see the same words.

content_fileCategoryWithCount.description: One entry in the note under a mod's file list saying how many files a hidden category holds.

content_filesNoneInActiveCategories.message: No files in the categories you have switched on. Hidden: $CATEGORIES$.
content_filesNoneInActiveCategories.description: Shown inside a mod's file list panel when every file it has belongs to a category the user has switched off in the filter bar.

content_filesNoneForMod.message: No files found for this mod.
content_filesNoneForMod.description: Shown inside a mod's file list panel when the mod has no downloadable files at all.

content_filesHiddenByFilters.description: Note under a mod's file list naming the categories that were left out, with a count for each.

content_fileCheckboxLabel.description: Screen reader name for the tick box beside one file in a mod's file list, naming the file and the category it is in.

content_fileFallbackName.description: Stands in for a file's name in the screen reader label when the file list gave no name.

content_fileMeta.description: The one-line detail under a file's name in a mod's file list: version, size and upload date. The 'v' prefixes the version number.

content_fileVersion.description: The version line under a file's name in the file picker dialog. The 'v' prefixes the version number.

content_fileSizeMb.description: A file's size in megabytes, shown in the detail line under its name in a mod's file list.

content_fileSizeKb.description: A file's size in kilobytes, shown in the detail line under its name in a mod's file list.

content_fileSizeUnknown.description: Stands in for a file's size in its detail line when Nexus reported no size.

content_fileDateUnknown.description: Stands in for a file's upload date in its detail line when Nexus reported no date.

content_downloadSelected.description: Button at the foot of a mod's file list, and the confirm button of the file picker dialog, that downloads the ticked files.

content_downloadSelectedCount.description: Bottom action bar button that downloads the ticked mods, with how many mods are ticked.

content_downloadSelectedModsFiles.description: Bottom action bar button that downloads the ticked mods, used when specific files were ticked so the file count is higher than the mod count.

content_downloadingProgress.description: Text of the Download Selected button inside a mod's file list while its files are being queued, counting progress.

content_downloadingEllipsis.description: Text of the bottom action bar's busy button while files picked from a single mod's file list are being queued.

content_fileOutcomeQueued.description: Result shown beside one file in a mod's file list after it was handed to the browser's downloads.

content_fileOutcomeFailed.description: Result shown beside one file in a mod's file list after its download could not be started.

content_reasonUnknown.description: Stands in for the cause of a failed download when nothing said why. Appears inside sentences such as 'Failed: unknown reason'.

content_filesQueuedOne.description: Status line under a mod's file list when exactly one file was handed to the browser's downloads. The count is always 1 here.

content_filesQueuedMany.description: Status line under a mod's file list when more than one file (or none) was handed to the browser's downloads.

content_filesQueuedWithFailures.description: Status line under a mod's file list when some downloads started and others did not.

content_panelTitle.description: Title in the filter bar the extension inserts above the mod grid. This is the product name and normally stays as it is.

content_panelSubtitle.description: Tagline under the product name in the filter bar, saying what the bar is for.

content_filtersRegionLabel.description: Screen reader name for the whole filter bar the extension inserts above the mod grid.

content_downloadsRegionLabel.description: Screen reader name for the action bar the extension fixes to the bottom of the page.

content_refresh.description: Button in the filter bar that reloads the page.

content_pageNavigation.description: Screen reader name for the group of Prev, page number and Next controls in the filter bar.

content_prevPage.description: Button in the filter bar that goes to the previous page of mod results. Kept short to fit the bar.

content_nextPage.description: Button in the filter bar that goes to the next page of mod results.

content_pageNumber.description: Screen reader name for the filter bar's page number box, which jumps to a page when a number is typed in it.

content_goToPage.description: Tooltip on the filter bar's page number box.

content_collapseFilters.description: Screen reader name of the filter bar's toggle button while the filters are showing; pressing it hides them.

content_expandFilters.description: Screen reader name of the filter bar's toggle button while the filters are hidden; pressing it shows them.

content_showUpdateFiles.description: Tooltip on the filter bar checkbox that includes or excludes files in the Update category.

content_showOptionalFiles.description: Tooltip on the filter bar checkbox that includes or excludes files in the Optional category.

content_showMiscFiles.description: Tooltip on the filter bar checkbox that includes or excludes files in the Miscellaneous category.

content_showOldFiles.message: Show old versions and archived files
content_showOldFiles.description: Tooltip on the filter bar checkbox that includes or excludes files in the Old and Archived categories.

content_exclusionLabel.description: Screen reader name for the filter bar text box that hides mods whose title contains any of the words typed in it.

content_exclusionPlaceholder.description: Gray hint text inside the empty filter bar box that hides mods by keyword. The words in brackets are examples the user might type.

content_exclusionTooltip.description: Tooltip on the filter bar box that hides mods by keyword, saying how to enter more than one word.

content_lastUpdatedRange.description: Screen reader name for the group of two date boxes in the filter bar that limit results by when a mod was last updated.

content_lastUpdatedLabel.description: Visible caption before the two date boxes in the filter bar.

content_updatedOnOrAfter.description: Screen reader name for the first date box in the filter bar, the start of the range.

content_updatedOnOrBefore.description: Screen reader name for the second date box in the filter bar, the end of the range.

content_startDateTooltip.description: Tooltip on the first date box in the filter bar, saying the date itself counts as a match.

content_endDateTooltip.description: Tooltip on the second date box in the filter bar, saying the date itself counts as a match.

content_clearDateRange.description: Tooltip and screen reader name of the small button beside the filter bar's date boxes that empties both of them.

content_clearButton.description: Visible text of the small button beside the filter bar's date boxes that empties both of them. Kept short to fit the bar.

content_noModsSelected.description: Label in the bottom action bar when the user has ticked no mod tiles.

content_modsSelectedOne.description: Label in the bottom action bar when exactly one mod tile is ticked. The count is always 1 here.

content_modsSelectedMany.description: Label in the bottom action bar showing how many mod tiles are ticked, used for counts other than one.

content_clearSelection.description: Button in the bottom action bar that unticks every selected mod.

content_clearSelectionTooltip.description: Tooltip on the Clear Selection button in the bottom action bar.

content_downloadAll.description: Button in the bottom action bar that downloads every mod currently visible in the grid, whether ticked or not.

content_downloadMode.description: Screen reader name and tooltip for the bottom action bar's dropdown that chooses between a plain browser download and handing the mod to the Vortex mod manager.

content_downloadModeManual.description: Option in the download mode dropdown: download the file through the browser.

content_downloadModeVortex.description: Option in the download mode dropdown: hand the mod to the Vortex mod manager. Vortex is a product name and stays as it is.

content_stopButton.description: Text the Download All button takes on while a download run is going, so the run can be halted from where it was started.

content_stopButtonTooltip.message: Stop the current download run. Files already started are not canceled.
content_stopButtonTooltip.description: Tooltip on the Stop button in the bottom action bar.

content_apiRemaining.description: Counter in the filter bar showing how many Nexus API requests the user's key has left.

content_selectMod.description: Visible label of the tick box the extension adds to each mod tile for batch downloading.

content_selectModNamed.description: Screen reader name for a mod tile's tick box, naming which mod it selects.

content_selectThisMod.description: Screen reader name for a mod tile's tick box before the tile's mod name is known.

content_summaryEntry.description: One line of the tally under the filter bar: a compatibility verdict and how many mods on the page got it.

content_summaryLastChecked.description: Small line under the tally naming the verdict of the most recently finished check.

content_preparingDownload.description: Badge text on a mod tile while its download is being set up.

content_downloadStarted.description: Note added to a mod tile's badge once the file was handed to the browser's downloads.

content_downloadStartedDetail.message: Check your browser downloads for the file.
content_downloadStartedDetail.description: Tooltip on a mod tile's badge after its download was started, saying where the file went.

content_downloadFailed.description: Badge text on a mod tile when its download could not be started.

content_noFileToDownload.message: Could not find a file to download
content_noFileToDownload.description: Badge text on a mod tile when looking up which file to download failed.

content_noDownloadableFile.description: Badge text on a mod tile when the mod offers no file the extension can download on its own.

content_noDownloadableFileDetail.message: This mod may not have a primary file or requires manual selection.
content_noDownloadableFileDetail.description: Tooltip explaining why no file could be downloaded automatically for a mod.

content_skippedAtFilePrompt.description: Badge text on a mod tile when the user closed the file picker dialog without choosing a file.

content_skippedAtFilePromptDetail.message: No file was chosen for this mod.
content_skippedAtFilePromptDetail.description: Tooltip on the 'Skipped at the file prompt' badge.

content_downloadRunStopped.description: Badge text on a mod tile that was never reached because the user stopped the batch download.

content_downloadRunStoppedDetail.message: The run ended before a file was chosen for this mod.
content_downloadRunStoppedDetail.description: Tooltip on the 'Download run stopped' badge.

content_vortexUnavailable.description: Badge text on a mod tile when no nxm:// link could be built to hand the mod to the Vortex mod manager.

content_vortexUnavailableDetail.message: Unable to resolve an NXM link. Ensure you are logged in to nexusmods.com.
content_vortexUnavailableDetail.description: Tooltip on the 'Vortex download unavailable' badge. NXM is the link type Vortex registers with the browser.

content_handedToVortex.description: Badge text on a mod tile after the browser passed the mod's link to the Vortex mod manager.

content_handedToVortexDetail.message: The browser passed an nxm:// link to Vortex. The browser cannot confirm Vortex received it.
content_handedToVortexDetail.description: Tooltip on the 'Handed to Vortex' badge, warning that success cannot be verified from the page.

content_vortexBlocked.description: Badge text on a mod tile when the browser refused to open the link that would reach the Vortex mod manager.

content_vortexBlockedDetail.message: The browser refused to open the nxm:// link.
content_vortexBlockedDetail.description: Tooltip on the 'Vortex handoff blocked' badge.

content_vortexHandoff.message: Sending these mods to Vortex over nxm:// links.
content_vortexHandoff.description: Notice shown once per session when a batch download runs in Vortex mode.

content_vortexHandoffDetail.message: Nothing happens if Vortex is not installed and registered for nxm links, and browsers may block repeated protocol launches from one click. Switch the mode to Manual if nothing arrives.
content_vortexHandoffDetail.description: Detail under the Vortex notice, saying why nothing may reach Vortex and what to do about it. 'Manual' is the other option in the download mode dropdown.

content_batchEmpty.message: Nothing to download: no mod matched the current selection and filters.
content_batchEmpty.description: Notice shown when a download run was started but had no mods to act on.

content_batchBusy.message: A download run is already in progress.
content_batchBusy.description: Notice shown when the user starts a download run while another one is still going.

content_batchVerbQueued.description: Verb used in the download run summary for files handed to the browser's downloads. Appears inside sentences such as '12 queued.'

content_batchVerbVortex.description: Verb used in the download run summary for mods passed to the Vortex mod manager. Appears inside sentences such as '12 handed to Vortex.'

content_batchSummary.description: Notice summarizing a download run in which nothing failed. The verb is content_batchVerbQueued or content_batchVerbVortex.

content_batchSummaryWithFailures.description: Notice summarizing a download run in which some mods failed. The verb is content_batchVerbQueued or content_batchVerbVortex.

content_batchFailureDetail.description: One entry in the detail line under a download run summary: the mod (and file) that failed, and why.

content_batchLabelDownloading.description: Name of the download run started by the Download Selected button. It is shown with a progress count, as in 'Downloading (3/12)...'

content_batchLabelDownloadingAll.description: Name of the download run started by the Download All button. It is shown with a progress count, as in 'Downloading all (3/12)...'

content_batchProgress.description: Text of the bottom action bar's busy button during a download run: the run's name plus how far it has got.

content_reasonAlreadyDownloading.description: Reason listed in a download run summary: the same file was already being downloaded.

content_reasonNoDownloadableFile.description: Reason listed in a download run summary: the mod offers no file the extension can download.

content_reasonRunStopped.description: Reason listed in a download run summary: the user stopped the run before this mod was reached.

content_reasonSkippedRequirements.description: Reason listed in a download run summary: the user chose Skip Mod in the dialog listing the mod's required mods.

content_reasonSkippedFilePrompt.description: Reason listed in a download run summary: the user closed the file picker dialog without choosing a file.

content_reasonFileListUnreadable.message: the file list could not be loaded
content_reasonFileListUnreadable.description: Reason listed in a download run summary: the mod's files could not be fetched.

content_reasonNoNxmLink.description: Reason listed in a download run summary: no nxm:// link could be built to hand the mod to the Vortex mod manager.

content_reasonNxmRefused.description: Reason listed in a download run summary: the browser would not open the link that reaches the Vortex mod manager.

content_reasonHiddenByFilters.description: Reason listed in a download run summary: by the time the run reached this mod, the filters had hidden its tile.

content_reasonAnotherRunInProgress.message: another download run is in progress
content_reasonAnotherRunInProgress.description: Reason shown beside each file in a mod's file list when the download could not start because a batch run was already going.

content_modalOk.description: Default text of a dialog's confirm button when the dialog names none of its own.

content_selectFilesTitle.description: Title of the dialog that asks which of a mod's files to download when more than one qualifies.

content_skipMod.description: Button that leaves this mod out of the download run and moves on to the next one.

content_skipThisMod.description: Button in the 'Could not verify requirements' dialog that leaves this one mod out of the download.

content_skipTheseMods.description: Button in the 'Could not verify requirements' dialog during a batch run, where the answer applies to every remaining mod in the run rather than just this one.

content_downloadAnyway.description: Button in the 'Could not verify requirements' dialog that downloads the mod despite not knowing what it requires.

content_requirementsUnverifiedTitle.description: Title of the dialog shown when the list of mods a mod requires could not be fetched. It means the check could not run, not that the mod has no requirements.

content_requirementsUnverifiedBody.message: $SUBJECT$ may have required mods, but the list could not be loaded: $REASON$
content_requirementsUnverifiedBody.description: Body of the 'Could not verify requirements' dialog. The subject is either the mod's name in quotes or the words 'This mod'.

content_requirementsUnverifiedRunNote.message: This usually fails for a whole run, so your answer is applied to the rest of it.
content_requirementsUnverifiedRunNote.description: Sentence appended to the 'Could not verify requirements' body during a batch download. It starts with a space because it follows the previous sentence directly.

content_requirementsIntro.message: $SUBJECT$ has the following requirements. Select which ones to install:
content_requirementsIntro.description: Opening line of the dialog listing the mods a mod requires. The subject is either the mod's name in quotes or the words 'This mod'.

content_thisMod.description: Stands in for a mod's name at the start of a sentence when the name is not known. Used as the subject of content_requirementsIntro and content_requirementsUnverifiedBody.

content_quotedModName.description: A mod's name in quotation marks, used as the subject of content_requirementsIntro and content_requirementsUnverifiedBody. Use whatever quotation marks the target language uses.

content_requirementsForMod.description: Title of the dialog listing the mods a named mod requires.

content_requirementsDetected.description: Title of the dialog listing the mods a mod requires, used when the mod's own name is not known.

content_installWithRequirements.description: Confirm button of the requirements dialog: download the mod and every ticked required mod.

content_installWithoutRequirements.description: Button in the requirements dialog: download only this mod and none of the mods it requires.

content_unknownMod.description: Stands in for a required mod's name in the requirements dialog when the mod page did not give one.

content_noLinkProvided.description: Stands in for a required mod's link in the requirements dialog when the mod page gave no address.

content_requirementsUnreadable.message: The requirements list could not be read.
content_requirementsUnreadable.description: Reason given when the answer to a request for a mod's required mods was not in a shape the extension could read.

content_requirementsPartial.description: Notice after the requirements dialog, saying how many of the required mods began downloading.

content_errorKeyRejected.message: Your Nexus API key was rejected. Re-enter it in the extension popup.
content_errorKeyRejected.description: Error shown on the page when Nexus refused the user's API key.

content_errorForbidden.message: Nexus refused this request. A premium account or an active nexusmods.com login may be required.
content_errorForbidden.description: Error shown on the page when Nexus refused a request the key was not entitled to make.

content_errorNotFound.message: This mod is not available (deleted, hidden, or wrong game).
content_errorNotFound.description: Error shown on the page when Nexus has no such mod.

content_errorRateLimited.message: Nexus API limit reached. Checks will resume after the limit resets.
content_errorRateLimited.description: Error shown on the page when the user's Nexus API quota is exhausted.

content_errorNexusDown.message: Nexus is not responding right now.
content_errorNexusDown.description: Error shown on the page when the Nexus servers returned a server-side failure.

content_errorOffline.description: Error shown on the page when the request never reached Nexus at all.

content_errorNoApiKey.message: No Nexus API key is set. Add one in the extension popup.
content_errorNoApiKey.description: Error shown on the page when a check needed an API key and none was saved.

content_errorUnexpected.description: Error shown on the page when a failure carried no message of its own.

content_errorPortTimeout.message: The check took too long and was abandoned.
content_errorPortTimeout.description: Error shown on the page when a compatibility check ran past its deadline.

content_errorNoBackground.message: Lost contact with the extension background. Retrying.
content_errorNoBackground.description: Error shown on the page when the page lost its connection to the extension's background service worker.

content_errorContextInvalid.message: The extension was updated. Reload this page.
content_errorContextInvalid.description: Error shown on the page when the extension was updated or reloaded while this page was open, which leaves the page's copy of it dead.

content_errorDisabled.description: Error shown on the page when a check was attempted while the extension is turned off.

content_errorCanceled.description: Error shown on the page when a compatibility check was called off before it finished.

content_errorUnknownMessaging.description: Error shown on the page when talking to the extension's background service worker failed and nothing said why.

content_errorTooManyRequests.description: Error shown on the page when the extension already has more checks in flight than it will hold.

content_errorBackground.description: Error shown on the page when the extension's background service worker failed and gave no message of its own.

content_shortKeyRejected.description: Very short reason shown on a compatibility badge beside 'Couldn't check': the Nexus API key was refused. Keep it to two or three words so it fits the badge.

content_shortAccessRefused.description: Very short reason shown on a compatibility badge beside 'Couldn't check': Nexus refused the request. Keep it to two or three words so it fits the badge.

content_shortNotAvailable.description: Very short reason shown on a compatibility badge beside 'Couldn't check': Nexus has no such mod. Keep it to two or three words so it fits the badge.

content_shortRateLimited.description: Very short reason shown on a compatibility badge beside 'Couldn't check': the Nexus API quota is exhausted. Keep it to two or three words so it fits the badge.

content_shortNexusDown.description: Very short reason shown on a compatibility badge beside 'Couldn't check': the Nexus servers failed. Keep it to two or three words so it fits the badge.

content_shortOffline.description: Very short reason shown on a compatibility badge beside 'Couldn't check': the request never reached Nexus. Keep it to two or three words so it fits the badge.

content_shortTimedOut.description: Very short reason shown on a compatibility badge beside 'Couldn't check': the check ran past its deadline. Keep it to two or three words so it fits the badge.

content_shortNoBackground.description: Very short reason shown on a compatibility badge beside 'Couldn't check': the page lost contact with the extension's background service worker. Keep it to two or three words so it fits the badge.

content_shortNeedsReload.description: Very short reason shown on a compatibility badge beside 'Couldn't check': the extension was updated and the page must be reloaded. Keep it to two or three words so it fits the badge.

content_shortSwitchedOff.description: Very short reason shown on a compatibility badge beside 'Couldn't check': the extension is turned off. Keep it to two or three words so it fits the badge.

content_shortCanceled.description: Very short reason shown on a compatibility badge beside 'Couldn't check': the check was called off. Keep it to two or three words so it fits the badge.

content_shortCheckFailed.description: Very short reason shown on a compatibility badge beside 'Couldn't check' when nothing more specific is known. Keep it to two or three words so it fits the badge.

content_shortRequestRefused.description: Very short reason shown on a compatibility badge beside 'Couldn't check': Nexus rejected the request as malformed. Keep it to two or three words so it fits the badge.

content_shortNotSetUp.description: Very short reason shown on a compatibility badge beside 'Couldn't check': no game version has been chosen yet. Keep it to two or three words so it fits the badge.

content_shortOtherGame.description: Very short reason shown on a compatibility badge beside 'Couldn't check': the mod belongs to a different game than the one set up. Keep it to two or three words so it fits the badge.

content_shortNoVersionDerived.description: Very short reason shown on a compatibility badge beside 'Couldn't check': no public source names a version for this game yet. This is a gap in the data, not a refusal. Keep it to two or three words so it fits the badge.

content_shortSuperseded.description: Very short reason shown on a compatibility badge beside 'Couldn't check': a newer check replaced this one. Keep it to two or three words so it fits the badge.

content_shortPageNotRecognized.description: Very short reason shown on a compatibility badge beside 'Couldn't check': the Nexus page was not in a layout the extension knows. Keep it to two or three words so it fits the badge.

content_dismiss.description: Screen reader name of the small close button on a notice the extension shows over the page.

content_reloadPage.description: Button on a notice that reloads the current Nexus page.

content_contextInvalidatedNotice.message: Nexus Mods Assistant was updated. Reload this page to continue.
content_contextInvalidatedNotice.description: Notice shown over the page when the extension was updated or reloaded while this page was open, so its copy of the extension has stopped working.

content_selectionRestoredOne.message: $COUNT$ mod you selected earlier is still selected.
content_selectionRestoredOne.description: Notice after a page load telling the user their one earlier tick was kept. The count is always 1 here.

content_selectionRestoredMany.message: $COUNT$ mods you selected earlier are still selected.
content_selectionRestoredMany.description: Notice after a page load telling the user their earlier ticks were kept, for counts other than one.

content_selectionRestoredDetail.message: Selections are kept for this tab until you clear them or close it.
content_selectionRestoredDetail.description: Detail under the restored-selection notice, saying how long the ticks last.

content_clearSelectionAction.description: Button on the restored-selection notice that unticks every mod at once.

content_selectionDroppedOne.message: $COUNT$ selected mod from another game was dropped.
content_selectionDroppedOne.description: Notice after moving to another game's pages, saying one tick could not be kept because a mod id only means something within its own game. The count is always 1 here.

content_selectionDroppedMany.message: $COUNT$ selected mods from another game were dropped.
content_selectionDroppedMany.description: Notice after moving to another game's pages, saying ticks could not be kept because a mod id only means something within its own game. Used for counts other than one.

content_noticeNoApiKey.message: Compatibility checks are off until you add a Nexus API key.
content_noticeNoApiKey.description: Notice shown on the page when no Nexus API key has been saved, so no verdicts can be computed.

content_noticeNoApiKeyDetail.message: Everything else on this page still works.
content_noticeNoApiKeyDetail.description: Detail under the missing-API-key notice, saying the rest of the extension is unaffected.

content_openSettings.description: Button on a notice that opens the extension's popup.

content_noticeOtherGame.message: Compatibility is set up for $TARGETGAME$, and this page is $PAGEGAME$.
content_noticeOtherGame.description: Notice shown when the game the user configured is not the game whose pages they are browsing. The values are Nexus game identifiers such as 'gamedomain'.

content_noticeNoTarget.message: Pick the game version you are playing to get compatibility badges.
content_noticeNoTarget.description: Notice shown when no game version has been chosen yet, so no verdicts can be computed.

content_noticeNotTargetedDetail.message: No verdicts are shown rather than verdicts computed against another game.
content_noticeNotTargetedDetail.description: Detail under the not-targeted notice, explaining that silence is deliberate.

content_useThisGame.description: Button on the not-targeted notice that opens the dialog for setting up the game shown on this page.

content_noticeOpenPopupManually.message: Open the Nexus Mods Assistant popup from your browser toolbar to change settings.
content_noticeOpenPopupManually.description: Notice shown when the page asked to open the extension's popup and the browser would not allow it.

content_targetModalTitle.description: Title of the dialog where the user says which build of the current game they play.

content_targetPromptQuestion.message: Which build of $GAME$ are you playing? Mods are judged against this version.
content_targetPromptQuestion.description: Question at the top of the 'Target this game' dialog. The value is a Nexus game identifier such as 'gamedomain'.

content_targetVersionPlaceholder.description: Gray hint text inside the empty version box of the 'Target this game' dialog, showing the shape of a version number.

content_targetVersionsDeriving.message: Deriving this game's versions from public sources...
content_targetVersionsDeriving.description: Status line in the 'Target this game' dialog while the extension looks for known versions of the game. One of three states this line can take, and it must not read like either of the others.

content_targetVersionsNone.message: No public source names a version for this game, so there is nothing to offer. Type the build you play if you know it.
content_targetVersionsNone.description: Status line in the 'Target this game' dialog when the search finished and found no versions. This means the search worked and there was nothing to find, unlike content_targetVersionsFailed, where the search itself did not complete.

content_targetVersionsFoundOne.message: $COUNT$ version was derived for this game. Open the list in the box above, or type your own.
content_targetVersionsFoundOne.description: Status line in the 'Target this game' dialog when exactly one version was found. The count is always 1 here.

content_targetVersionsFoundMany.message: $COUNT$ versions were derived for this game. Open the list in the box above, or type your own.
content_targetVersionsFoundMany.description: Status line in the 'Target this game' dialog when more than one version was found.

content_targetVersionsFailed.message: The version search could not complete ($REASON$), so this list is empty for want of an answer, not for want of data. Type the build you play.
content_targetVersionsFailed.description: Status line in the 'Target this game' dialog when the search itself failed. This means the extension could not look, unlike content_targetVersionsNone, where it looked and found nothing.

content_save.description: Confirm button of the 'Target this game' dialog.

content_cancel.description: Button that closes the 'Target this game' dialog without saving.

content_targetNotSaved.message: No version was entered, so nothing was saved and this page is still untargeted.
content_targetNotSaved.description: Notice shown when the user pressed Save in the 'Target this game' dialog with the version box empty.

content_targetNotSavedDetail.message: Pick one of the derived versions, or type the build you play.
content_targetNotSavedDetail.description: Detail under the nothing-was-saved notice, saying what to do instead.

content_tryAgain.description: Button on the nothing-was-saved notice that reopens the 'Target this game' dialog.

content_noModsOnPage.description: Notice shown when the Nexus search returned no results. This is an empty result, not a failure.

content_layoutStillLoading.message: The mod list has not finished loading. If it stays this way, Nexus may have changed their layout.
content_layoutStillLoading.description: Notice shown when the mod grid is present but still empty, which could be a slow page or a change to the Nexus markup.

content_layoutNotFound.message: Could not find the mod list on this page. Nexus may have changed their layout.
content_layoutNotFound.description: Notice shown when no mod grid could be found on the page at all.

content_layoutBrokenSelectors.description: Detail under a layout notice, naming the parts of the page the extension could no longer find. The names are internal identifiers and are not translated.

content_layoutSelectorGrid.description: Stands in for the list of missing page parts when the mod grid itself is the only thing that could not be found. It appears inside content_layoutBrokenSelectors alongside untranslated identifiers.

content_detailLayoutUnrecognized.message: This mod page does not look like a layout the assistant recognizes, so no badge was added.
content_detailLayoutUnrecognized.description: Notice shown on an individual mod page whose markup the extension does not know, so it added no compatibility badge.

content_translationSignalMissing.message: Translations are set to be hidden, but no mod tile on this page says what category it is in, so nothing was hidden.
content_translationSignalMissing.description: Notice shown when the setting to hide translation mods could not be applied because the page exposes no category for any tile.

content_translationSignalMissingDetail.message: Nexus may have changed their markup. Nothing has been hidden from you.
content_translationSignalMissingDetail.description: Detail under the translations-not-hidden notice, reassuring the user that no results were removed.

content_dateFilterNotApplied.message: The date filter is not being applied: no mod tile on this page exposes an update date.
content_dateFilterNotApplied.description: Note under the filter bar saying the Last Updated range had no dates to test against.

content_dateSelectorBroken.message: The "Last Updated" filter could not read any dates on this page, so it was not applied.
content_dateSelectorBroken.description: Notice saying the Last Updated range was ignored because no tile on the page carries a date. The quoted name matches the filter bar's own Last Updated caption.

content_dateSelectorBrokenDetail.message: Nexus may have changed their markup.
content_dateSelectorBrokenDetail.description: Detail under the date-filter notice, naming the likely cause.

content_undatedHiddenOne.message: $COUNT$ mod hidden: no update date to test against.
content_undatedHiddenOne.description: Note under the filter bar counting the one mod hidden by the date range because it carries no date. The count is always 1 here.

content_undatedHiddenMany.message: $COUNT$ mods hidden: no update date to test against.
content_undatedHiddenMany.description: Note under the filter bar counting the mods hidden by the date range because they carry no date. Used for counts other than one.

content_translationsHiddenOne.message: $COUNT$ translation mod hidden by the popup setting.
content_translationsHiddenOne.description: Note under the filter bar counting the one translation mod hidden by the extension's setting. The count is always 1 here.

content_translationsHiddenMany.message: $COUNT$ translation mods hidden by the popup setting.
content_translationsHiddenMany.description: Note under the filter bar counting the translation mods hidden by the extension's setting. Used for counts other than one.

content_rescanDeferred.message: Settings changed. The badges refresh once the current download run finishes.
content_rescanDeferred.description: Notice shown when the user changed settings during a download run, so the badges are not repainted until the run is over.

popup_appName.description: The product name. It is the popup window's document title and the heading at the top left of the popup. This is a brand name: keep it as it is unless the language needs a transliteration.

popup_subtitle.description: The line under the popup heading. "Alkeari Labs LLC" is a company name and never changes; only "Compatibility Companion", the tagline, is translated.

popup_extensionToggle.description: Tooltip and screen reader label for the on/off switch at the top right of the popup, which turns the whole extension on or off.

popup_sectionGameVersion.description: Heading of the first card in the popup, where the user picks the game and the game version range their mods must be compatible with.

popup_suggestedGameDefault.message: The tab you have open is a Nexus game page.
popup_suggestedGameDefault.description: Placeholder sentence in the hidden suggestion row at the top of the first card. At runtime it is replaced by popup_openTabIsGame, which names the game.

popup_useThisGame.description: Button next to the suggestion row. It selects the game of the Nexus page the user has open in a browser tab.

popup_gameLabel.description: Label of the text box where the user searches the Nexus game catalog by title.

popup_gameSearchPlaceholder.description: Placeholder inside the game search box, shown while it is empty.

popup_gameSuggestionsLabel.description: Screen reader label for the drop-down list of games matching what was typed in the game search box.

popup_versionRangeLabel.description: Label above the pair of boxes where the user enters the earliest and latest game version a mod must support.

popup_versionMinAriaLabel.description: Screen reader label for the first of the two version boxes, the start of the range.

popup_versionMinPlaceholder.description: Placeholder in the start-of-range version box. 1.3.8 is a sample version number and stays as it is.

popup_versionMaxAriaLabel.description: Screen reader label for the second of the two version boxes, the optional end of the range.

popup_versionMaxPlaceholder.description: Placeholder in the end-of-range version box, which the user may leave empty.

popup_versionSuggestionsLabel.description: Screen reader label for the drop-down list of game version numbers the extension found on public web sources.

popup_refreshVersions.description: Button under the version boxes. It searches public sources again for this game's version numbers.

popup_refreshVersionsTitle.message: Search the public sources again for this game's versions
popup_refreshVersionsTitle.description: Tooltip on the Refresh versions button.

popup_exclusionLabel.description: Label of the box where the user types keywords; mods whose titles contain them are hidden from Nexus listings.

popup_exclusionPlaceholder.description: Placeholder in the exclusion keywords box, showing two sample keywords separated by a comma.

popup_exclusionTitle.description: Tooltip on the exclusion keywords box.

popup_hideTranslationsTitle.message: Adds Nexus's own translation filter to the listing this button opens
popup_hideTranslationsTitle.description: Tooltip on the checkbox that excludes translation mods from the listing the popup opens.

popup_hideTranslations.message: Open the listing with translations excluded
popup_hideTranslations.description: Label of the checkbox that excludes translation mods from the Nexus listing the popup opens.

popup_openCompatibleMods.description: The main button of the popup. It opens a Nexus mod listing for the selected game in a new tab.

popup_sectionConnection.description: Heading of the card where the user stores or removes their Nexus API key.

popup_apiKeyLabel.description: Label of the read-only box showing the stored API key, masked until the user reveals it.

popup_apiKeyDisplayAriaLabel.description: Screen reader label for the read-only box showing the stored API key.

popup_revealKey.description: Tooltip and screen reader label on the Show button, while the stored key is masked.

popup_hideKey.description: Tooltip and screen reader label on the same button once the key is on screen, so pressing it masks the key again.

popup_show.description: Small button next to the stored API key. It reveals the masked key. Keep it short: the button is narrow.

popup_hide.description: The same small button once the key is revealed. Pressing it masks the key again. Keep it short: the button is narrow.

popup_replaceKey.description: Button that opens the entry box so the user can paste a different Nexus API key.

popup_disconnect.description: Button that starts removing the stored Nexus API key, and the confirming button in the panel it opens.

popup_disconnectExplain.message: Disconnect removes the key and every cached Nexus response from this browser. Your Nexus account is untouched.
popup_disconnectExplain.description: Explanation shown in the confirmation panel before the stored API key is removed.

popup_keepKey.description: Button that cancels the disconnect confirmation and leaves the stored key in place.

popup_apiKeyInputLabel.description: Label of the password box where the user pastes a Nexus API key. "Personal API Key" is the name Nexus itself uses on its settings page.

popup_apiKeyPlaceholder.description: Placeholder in the box where the user pastes a Nexus API key.

popup_save.description: Button that stores the API key the user pasted. Keep it short: the button sits beside the entry box.

popup_needKey.description: Button that opens the Nexus website page where an API key is generated.

popup_cancel.description: Button that abandons entering a replacement API key and returns to the stored key view.

popup_connectionOptionalNote.message: Optional. Browsing, filters and the version target work without one. Compatibility badges and downloads need a key, because Nexus only answers for an account.
popup_connectionOptionalNote.description: Note under the API key entry box, saying which features work without a key.

popup_ssoHeading.description: Heading of the block offering to fetch an API key by signing in to Nexus Mods instead of pasting one.

popup_ssoDescription.message: Authorize once and the key is filled in for you. You can run this again at any time to replace the stored key.
popup_ssoDescription.description: Explanation under the single sign-on heading.

popup_authorizeSso.description: Button that starts the Nexus Mods single sign-on handshake. SSO is the usual abbreviation of single sign-on.

popup_cancelSso.description: The same button while a single sign-on handshake is running. Pressing it abandons the handshake.

popup_ssoReady.message: Ready to start the Nexus Mods SSO handshake.
popup_ssoReady.description: Status line under the single sign-on button before anything has been started.

popup_startingSso.description: Status line under the single sign-on button the moment the handshake is requested.

popup_ssoCanceled.description: Status line under the single sign-on button after the user cancels the handshake.

popup_sectionDownloads.description: Heading of the card holding the download mode and the file list category switches.

popup_downloadModeLabel.description: Label of the drop-down that chooses what happens when the user downloads a mod file.

popup_downloadModeManual.message: Manual: the browser saves the file
popup_downloadModeManual.description: First option of the download mode drop-down: the browser downloads the file itself.

popup_downloadModeVortex.message: Vortex: your mod manager takes the link
popup_downloadModeVortex.description: Second option of the download mode drop-down. Vortex is the name of a mod manager application and stays as it is.

popup_downloadModeNoteBefore.message: The same setting as the one in the action bar on a Nexus listing page: changing it here changes it there, and the other way round. Vortex mode opens an
popup_downloadModeNoteBefore.description: First half of the note under the download mode drop-down. The full sentence reads: "... Vortex mode opens an nxm:// link, which your operating system hands to whichever mod manager registered that protocol." The literal nxm:// sits between this string and popup_downloadModeNoteAfter, in a monospace style, so this half must end where the link name begins.

popup_downloadModeNoteAfter.message: link, which your operating system hands to whichever mod manager registered that protocol.
popup_downloadModeNoteAfter.description: Second half of the note under the download mode drop-down, following the literal nxm:// that ends popup_downloadModeNoteBefore.

popup_fileListsLegend.description: Heading of the group of switches choosing which file categories are shown in a mod's file list.

popup_fileListsNote.message: Which file categories appear when a mod's file list is opened. The same four switches sit in the on-page panel.
popup_fileListsNote.description: Note under the File lists heading, saying that the same switches appear in the panel the extension draws on Nexus pages.

popup_showOldFilesTitle.message: Show older versions of a mod's files
popup_showOldFilesTitle.description: Tooltip on the Old files switch.

popup_showOldFiles.description: Label of the switch that shows the Old files category in a mod's file list. It is the category name Nexus itself uses.

popup_showUpdateFilesTitle.description: Tooltip on the Update files switch.

popup_showUpdateFiles.description: Label of the switch that shows the Update files category in a mod's file list. It is the category name Nexus itself uses.

popup_showOptionalFilesTitle.description: Tooltip on the Optional files switch.

popup_showOptionalFiles.description: Label of the switch that shows the Optional files category in a mod's file list. It is the category name Nexus itself uses.

popup_showMiscFilesTitle.description: Tooltip on the Miscellaneous files switch.

popup_showMiscFiles.description: Label of the switch that shows the Miscellaneous files category in a mod's file list. It is the category name Nexus itself uses.

popup_sectionAdvanced.description: Heading of the last card, holding verbose logging and the cache clearing button.

popup_advancedNote.message: Local storage and diagnostics. Clearing the cache re-reads the game list from Nexus straight away when a key is connected; nothing else here reaches the network.
popup_advancedNote.description: Note under the Advanced heading, saying what the controls in that card do.

popup_debugLoggingTitle.message: Writes detailed background worker activity to the service worker console
popup_debugLoggingTitle.description: Tooltip on the verbose logging switch. "Service worker console" is the browser's own developer tools term.

popup_debugLogging.description: Label of the switch that makes the extension's background write detailed diagnostics to the browser console.

popup_clearCache.description: Button that deletes every Nexus answer the extension has stored on this computer. Its wording is quoted inside popup_storageFull and popup_keyRemovedWithLeftovers, so translate all three the same way.

popup_sourceStorePatchNote.description: Where a derived game version came from, shown as a small tag beside the version number in the suggestions list: a patch note published on the game's store page.

popup_sourceStoreBranch.description: Where a derived game version came from, shown as a small tag beside the version number: a named build branch on the game's store page.

popup_sourceArticleText.description: Where a derived game version came from, shown as a small tag beside the version number: a number read out of the body of a news article, which may not be a real build number.

popup_sourceModText.description: Where a derived game version came from, shown as a small tag beside the version number: the text of mod pages that name the version.

popup_sourceCollectionMetadata.description: Where a derived game version came from, shown as a small tag beside the version number: the metadata of a Nexus mod collection. "Collection" is a Nexus feature name.

popup_provenanceCorroboration.description: The small tag beside a derived version number when more than one source reported it: the source names followed by how many sources agreed, for example "store patch note x3".

popup_versionOptionAriaLabel.description: Screen reader label for one row of the derived versions list: the version number and where it came from.

popup_gameSuggestionRow.description: One row of the game search suggestions: the game's title followed by its Nexus web address name in parentheses.

popup_failureNoApiKey.message: No API key is connected, so Nexus will not answer. Add one under Connection.
popup_failureNoApiKey.description: Error line shown when a request needed an API key and none is stored. "Connection" is the popup card named by popup_sectionConnection: use the same wording.

popup_failureInvalidKey.message: Nexus rejected your API key. Replace it under Connection.
popup_failureInvalidKey.description: Error line shown when Nexus refuses the stored API key. "Connection" is the popup card named by popup_sectionConnection: use the same wording.

popup_failureForbidden.message: Nexus refused the request. A premium account or an active nexusmods.com login may be required.
popup_failureForbidden.description: Error line shown when Nexus answers that the request is not allowed for this account.

popup_failureNotFound.message: Nexus has no record of that game or mod. It may have been hidden or removed.
popup_failureNotFound.description: Error line shown when Nexus reports that the requested game or mod does not exist.

popup_failureRateLimited.message: You have used up your Nexus API allowance. Checks resume once it resets, usually within the hour.
popup_failureRateLimited.description: Error line shown when Nexus refuses further requests because the account's hourly request allowance is spent.
